behaviour: Internal hook that drives a data hook's retry from notification signals, with a polling fallback, one throttle and no overlapping refresh.
rules: Module constants: ThrottleDelayMs = 2000 and DefaultPollIntervalMs = 60_000.

Import useSignal from '@backstage/plugin-signals-react'. It returns { lastSignal: JsonObject | null; isSignalsAvailable: boolean }. Call useSignal('notifications') without a generic, as NotificationsPage does.

Hold a pending boolean in useState and create one throttled setter with useMemo(() => throttle(setPending, ThrottleDelayMs), []); throttle is the default lodash/throttle, so leading and trailing edges both fire.
An effect with cleanup calls the throttled setter's cancel() on unmount.
An effect runs retry() and then setPending(false) only when pending is true and loading is false, so no refresh starts while one is running.
An effect calls the throttled setter with true when lastSignal && lastSignal.action.
An effect returns undefined when isSignalsAvailable is true; otherwise it starts setInterval calling the throttled setter with true every pollIntervalMs, and its cleanup clears the interval.
requestRefresh is a useCallback over the same throttled setter, so a manual request shares the throttle window with signals.

params.name: options
params.type: { loading: boolean; retry: () => void; pollIntervalMs?: number }

behaviour: Home page card that lists the signed-in user's latest unread notifications, with mark-as-read and a deep link on each row.
rules: Props default to limit = 5, and pollIntervalMs passes through to the hook unset, so the hook's default applies.
Load with useNotificationsApi(api => api.getNotifications({ read: false, limit, sort: 'created', sortOrder: 'desc' }), [limit]).
Hold rows in useState<Notification[]>() and copy value.notifications into it from an effect only when value is set, so a failed refresh, which clears value, leaves rows in place.
Call useNotificationsRefresh({ loading, retry, pollIntervalMs }) and keep requestRefresh.
Render Card with className styles.card, CardHeader holding <Text as="h3" variant="title-x-small">{t('unreadCard.title')}</Text>, and CardBody, all from @backstage/ui.

CardBody content, first match wins: rows with items gives ul.list of rows; rows empty gives Text t('unreadCard.emptyState'); no rows and error gives <Alert status="danger" title={t('unreadCard.errors.loadFailed')} /> from @backstage/ui; otherwise Progress from @backstage/core-components.
Each row is a file-local UnreadNotificationRow in li.item: the severity span, then div.text holding the title and the time, then the mark-as-read control.
Severity: span.severity with role="img" and aria-label t(`filters.severity.${severity}`) around SeverityIcon, where severity is notification.payload.severity ?? 'normal'.

Title: <Text variant="body-medium" as="div" className={styles.title}> around Link from @backstage/core-components, whose to is `${notificationsRoute}?id=${encodeURIComponent(notification.id)}` and whose children are notification.payload.title. notification.payload.link is never read.
Time: <Text variant="body-small" color="secondary" as="div"> around <RelativeTime value={notification.created} />, imported with the // @ts-ignore line NotificationsTable uses.
notificationsRoute comes from useRouteRef(rootRouteRef)() in the card and is passed to rows as a prop.

Mark-as-read control: TooltipTrigger, ButtonIcon with aria-label t('unreadCard.markAsRead'), icon <RiCheckboxCircleLine size={16} />, variant secondary, isDisabled while the call runs, and Tooltip, as in BulkActions.

The row runs the call with useAsyncFn from react-use: await notificationsApi.updateNotifications({ ids: [notification.id], read: true }) and then onMarkedRead(notification.id); on a rejected call use the decided toast and leave the row.
onMarkedRead in the card returns at once when useMountedState() from react-use reports unmounted; otherwise it removes the id from rows with a functional setRows and calls requestRefresh().

behaviour: Covers the card's states, mark-as-read, deep links, signal refresh, the polling fallback and cleanup.
rules: Render with renderInTestApp(<TestApiProvider apis={...}><UnreadNotificationsCard /></TestApiProvider>, { mountedRoutes: { '/notifications': rootRouteRef } }). Always register notificationsApiRef and toastApiRef mocks; toast is { post: jest.fn() }.

The fake signal API is { subscribe: jest.fn((_channel, onMessage) => { emit = onMessage; return { unsubscribe }; }) } registered under signalApiRef from @backstage/plugin-signals-react. Leave it out to make signals unavailable. Each emit passes a new object such as { action: 'new_notification', notification_id: 'x' }.
Timer cases call jest.useFakeTimers() before rendering, restore real timers in afterEach, and advance time with await act(async () => { jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms); }).
Press the mark-as-read button with fireEvent.click from @testing-library/react; user-event is not a dependency of this package.
In the mark-as-read success case, later getNotifications calls resolve to an empty list, because the card refreshes after marking.
For the loading state use a getNotifications promise that stays pending and findByTestId('progress'), the id Progress already has.
